summary: Shard synchronization ripple after idle-stream resume causing p95/p99 latency spikes for short streaming requests
description:
Issue summary:
Acuity Health (dedicated customer) reports recurring p95/p99 latency spikes for short streaming requests (average 8-20 tokens) that correlate with many idle streams resuming simultaneously. Symptoms started 2026-03-11 after an increase in client keep-alive timeouts from their edge.

Impact:
- Intermittent higher-than-SLO tail latency (p95 up to 480ms, p99 up to 1.4s) on text-streaming endpoints for short sessions.
- Customers observe streaming stutters and occasional 504s when spikes coincide with backend flush delays.
- Affects ~7% of requests for Acuity Health during peak resume windows.

Environment:
- Redwood Dedicated pool: rwd-dedicated-us-east-2, serving-runtime v3.8.1, continuous-batcher enabled, 8 shards active.
- Traffic pattern: many low-QPS websocket connections with intermittent resume bursts (every ~90s).

Steps to reproduce (internal):
1. Create 1k short streaming connections (8-20 token workloads) and hold idle for 60-120s to simulate keep-alive behavior.
2. Trigger simultaneous resumes (send prompt) from all connections.
3. Observe batcher/shard flush timing and downstream latencies.
4. Compare against steady-state continuous traffic.

Observed behavior:
- When large numbers of idle connections resume, we see staggered tick alignment across continuous-batcher shards causing a ripple: some shards flush microbatches immediately while others wait for their next tick, producing a cascade of larger-than-normal flushes and transient queueing at the shard level.
- Short requests disproportionately affected because padding/coalescing decisions change when shards realign, which increases head-of-line wait for the smallest sequences.
- Logs show correlated "flush_delay" spikes and a wave pattern in per-shard flush timestamps (see investigation).

Expected behavior:
- Smooth batching with bounded per-request latency for short streams; graceful leveling across shards without multi-shard flush ripple.

Relevant logs/metrics snapshots:
- Grafana panels: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abc123/continuous-batcher?orgId=1&from=1647086400000&to=1647087000000
- Sample log excerpt (serving-runtime):
  [2026-03-11T17:02:05.112Z] shard-3 flush_delay=12ms queue_len=14
  [2026-03-11T17:02:05.116Z] shard-7 flush_delay=142ms queue_len=68
  [2026-03-11T17:02:05.118Z] shard-1 flush_delay=8ms queue_len=9
  [2026-03-11T17:02:05.217Z] shard-7 flush_delay=612ms queue_len=120 <-- correlated p99 spike

Notes:
- Similar but not identical to previous batcher issues (see linked tickets). This appears to be a shard synchronization/resonance phenomenon rather than simple linger/timeout misconfiguration.

investigation_notes:
Hypotheses:
1) Batcher shard tick alignment: when many idle streams resume at roughly the same time, internal timers (tick boundaries) across shards can align so that some shards immediately flush while others wait for the next tick boundary, producing a ripple of flushes and transient queueing.
2) Small-request unfairness: current coalescer weighting favors filling microbatch size thresholds which, under shard misalignment, starves short sequences until the next tick.
3) Flow-control/backpressure interaction: proxy-level TCP-window and the serving-runtime backpressure interplay amplify the flush ripple effect.

Evidence collected:
- Per-shard flush timestamps show a wave pattern with ~5-600ms separation between earliest and latest flush in the same resume window.
- CPU and GPU utilization remained moderate; not a hardware saturation issue.
- Replaying the resume burst in staging reproduces the p99 tails when tick alignment is synchronized across shards.

Experiment attempts:
- Forced randomized shard tick offsets in staging decreased p99 by ~60% for short streams.
- Increasing microbatch timeout from 20ms to 40ms reduced some 504s but increased average latency; tradeoff unacceptable for customer SLOs.
next_steps:
1) Create a short-term server-side mitigation to add jittered tick offsets across shards in production (rollout to one dedicated pool).
2) Add telemetry to measure per-resume-window flush dispersion and auto-detect ripple events.
3) Longer-term: evaluate coalescer fairness improvements that prioritize short sequences during resume bursts.
4) Schedule a postmortem and customer-facing incident summary after mitigation rollout.
workaround: Customer advised to add randomized client resume jitter (100-300ms) as an immediate mitigation. This reduced occurrence of mass-synchronized resumes in early tests. Provided a small JS snippet to implement jitter on reconnect.
resolution: (Pending) Short-term mitigation proposal reviewed. Plan to deploy randomized shard tick offsets to a single dedicated pool as a canary 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC. If canary reduces p99 by >50% without regressions, roll out to remaining dedicated pools. Final resolution will include coalescer fairness work and a follow-up release note.
